title: safeFetch checks DNS in a pre-flight lookup, then fetch resolves again: a rebinding window
instrument: a probe that runs fetchImageBase64 through an undici Agent whose connect.lookup is the injected Resolver, with a resolver answering a public address on the 1st lookup and 127.0.0.1 on the 2nd; arm A connects to the 2nd answer, arm B (validate inside connect.lookup) refuses
body:
## Summary
lib/imaging/safeUrl.ts validates a hostname's addresses with its own lookup, then hands the URL to fetch, which performs a second, unchecked lookup.

## Description
The header (lib/imaging/safeUrl.ts:25-27) says the resolved check is done 'at connect time, because a name under an attacker's control can point anywhere and can be changed between two lookups'. The code does exactly two lookups: assertFetchable's `resolve(host)` (lib/imaging/safeUrl.ts:166) and the platform fetch's own resolution inside `fetch(target, ...)` (lib/imaging/safeUrl.ts:198). A hostname with a zero TTL that answers public first and 127.0.0.1 / 169.254.169.254 second passes the check and connects to the private address. Fixed looks like: validation inside the socket's lookup (an undici `Agent({ connect: { lookup } })` dispatcher passed to fetch) so the address checked is the address connected to; the pre-flight check can stay for the literal/scheme rules. Registry: none governs SSRF here; repo convention (the header's own claim).

## Flow
- vendor response carries https://rebind.attacker.example/plate.png
- assertFetchable -> lookup #1 -> 93.184.216.34 -> admitted
- fetch -> lookup #2 -> 127.0.0.1 -> connects to loopback, body returned as base64

## Expected impact
Closes the one SSRF path the header claims is closed. Could break: a CDN whose addresses the custom lookup mis-handles (family/all options); the probe must cover v4 and v6 answers.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the address validated is the address connected to
Before: two lookups per hop; the second unchecked (read from the code; no probe can drive it without a dispatcher seam)
After: one lookup per hop, inside connect; a rebinding resolver is refused
Method: simulation - the platform fetch's internal lookup cannot be injected without adding an undici dispatcher, which is the change itself
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
drain_note: security: needs undici as a dependency (operator decision) to pin the connect lookup

title: Two rules for 'when will this fit': the 402 Retry-After vs budgetQuote.resumeAt
instrument: imaging-budget-forecast cases: $0.99 spent as [$0.001 at T-59s, $0.989 at T-1s] under $1 with a $0.045 refusal - Retry-After/earliestExpiry vs budgetQuote resumeAt; and a window blocked by holds only
body:
## Summary
earliestExpiry (lib/imaging/budgetForecast.ts:117-124) answers the 402's Retry-After and frames' imageFailure with the first row to age out, whatever it frees; budgetQuote computes when enough ages out.

## Description
errorResponse (lib/imaging/api.ts, status 402 branch) and lib/producers/frames.ts:330 both read earliestExpiry, which returns the earliest expiry of ANY booked row. A window whose oldest row is $0.001 tells the caller to retry when $0.001 frees, and the retry is refused again. budgetQuote (lib/imaging/budgetForecast.ts:80-95) already walks rows until remaining + expiring covers the estimate. And when the window is full of HOLDS with no booked rows, earliestExpiry says now + windowMs (an hour) and budgetQuote says resumeAt null, though holds release when the in-flight calls settle. Fixed: one function answers both, given the refused amount (carried on the over-budget error), and holds-only windows say so instead of a full window.

## Flow
- $0.001 booked at T-59s, $0.989 at T-1s, ceiling $1, window 60s
- generate refused 402; Retry-After = 1s
- retry at T+1s refused again; true resume is T+59s

## Expected impact
A caller that honours Retry-After stops being refused on its own retry. Could break: the error must carry the refused amount (an ImagingError field) - in-tree only.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one answer to 'when will this fit'
Before: 2 implementations that disagree on the walked case (1s vs 59s)
After: 1 implementation; both readers get 59s
Method: simulation - walked from the two functions; the forecast probe can pin both in S
Result: better
Gate: none

title: An estimate-basis spend row does not record the price row it was costed with
instrument: a meter-conformance case: book a served google call at basis estimate, change the PRICES row's checked date, assert the booked row still names the price it used (provider/model/checked)
body:
## Summary
SpendRow (lib/imaging/budget.ts:144-156) carries usd and basis but not which PRICES row (or which `checked` revision) produced an estimated figure.

## Description
cost-metering's golden path, 'The price table is versioned data with a loud default': a row costed at write time must remain explicable after the table changes, so it records what it was costed with. The router books `served.provenance.costUsd ?? standInUsd()` (lib/imaging/router.ts settle on the served branch) with basis 'estimate' and nothing else; standInUsd is estimatePerImage's dearest row, whose identity is lost at booking. After a repricing nobody can tell which rate a window's estimates used. The row shape lives in lib/spend/meter.ts (another context), so this is out-of-scope for this round.

## Flow
- served google call, costBasis estimated -> row {usd: 0.045, basis: estimate}
- PRICES google row repriced and re-dated
- window total can no longer be reconciled to a rate

## Expected impact
Spend rows become reconcilable against a repriced table. Could break: the persisted ledger file shape (additive field; old rows read as unknown).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every estimated row names its rate
Before: 0 of N estimate rows name the price row
After: N of N
Method: simulation - the row shape is the spend kernel's (lib/spend/meter.ts), outside this context's paths
Result: better
Gate: contract

title: pricing.ts's no-env invariant has no guard since DELIBERATELY_PUBLIC emptied
instrument: a case in imaging-auth (or imaging-budget) running the existing transitive no-env import walk over lib/imaging/pricingHandler.ts directly, seeded red by adding an env read to pricing.ts
body:
## Summary
pricing.ts and budget.ts both rely on 'pricing.ts reads no process.env and imports nothing that does'; the only walk that asserted it ran over DELIBERATELY_PUBLIC routes, and that list is now {}.

## Description
lib/imaging/pricing.ts header (the no-env rule) and lib/imaging/budget.ts:21-25 ('does NOT compromise pricing.ts's no-env property') state the invariant; tests/golden-path/imaging-auth.probe.spec.ts:82-85 says the pricing route retired and the walk 'runs over it again' only when a public route is admitted. Until then nothing fails if pricing.ts imports env.ts. Fixed: the walk runs over pricingHandler.ts unconditionally.

## Flow
- add `import { currentEnv } from './env'` to pricing.ts
- npm test stays green today
- with the case: red

## Expected impact
The rule a future public price route depends on is held by a test, not by a comment. Nothing can break; it is a test.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a stated invariant has a guard
Before: 0 guards (DELIBERATELY_PUBLIC = {})
After: 1 guard, seeded red
Method: simulation - the walk lives in imaging-auth, another context's probe; not built this round
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Unpriced non-USD providers (agy, leonardo-studio) book the dearest USD rate into the USD window
body:
## Summary
A served agy or leonardo-studio call arrives with costUsd undefined, and the router books standInUsd() = $0.045 x N as an 'estimate' against the imaging USD ceiling, though neither spends USD.

## Description
lib/imaging/router.ts standInUsd excludes only `recognize` (per-token). agy bills its own CLI plan quota and leonardo-studio prepaid studio credits (lib/imaging/pricing.ts rows; providers/leonardoStudio.ts:13-22 states the over-read and calls it 'erring high'). A scout night drawing 30 studio stills books $1.35 of USD spend that never happened, refusing Google work the operator could afford. The registry (cost-metering, unit-classes-are-open) argues for a separate class per unit rather than a USD stand-in. Booking less is a loosening of the spend guard, so it is the operator's call.

## Flow
- 30 leonardo-studio stills in one window
- 30 x $0.045 = $1.35 booked as USD estimate
- a later Google generate is refused at the $5 ceiling sooner

## Expected impact
USD ceiling reflects USD. Risk: an agy/studio call that DOES cost USD would no longer be counted.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the USD window counts USD
Before: N studio/agy calls book N x $0.045 USD
After: 0 USD booked; their own unit counted in its own class
Method: simulation - read from router.ts and the provider headers; the change books less, which is policy-loosen
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: policy-loosen
